findings.title: Portable Run address proof still accepts Windows reserved device names
findings.problem: The revised Explore separates logical Run occurrence identity from physical addressing and independently closes traversal/separator/absolute/drive/UNC cases. However its conservative lowercase-ASCII-token physical-segment gate still accepts values such as con, prn, aux, nul, com1 and lpt1. Those values pass path.win32 basename/normalize/join containment checks but are reserved Win32 device names, so the proof does not yet establish the claimed portable canonical repository segment.
reviewEvidence: Reviewer independently reproduced the declared 18 path cases: 18/18 PASS.
Under the described candidate grammar/gate, con, prn, aux, nul, com1, com9, lpt1 and lpt9 are all accepted.
Microsoft Win32 naming rules reserve CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-COM9 and LPT1-LPT9 as device names.
requiredRevision: Extend R7 / path-address contract to cover Windows reserved device basenames as a portability/canonical-address risk.
Either require a physical address representation that structurally cannot equal a reserved device name, or explicitly reject reserved device basenames case-insensitively before filesystem use.
Add controlled negative proof for the reserved device-name class while preserving acceptance of canonical current dated Action segments.
Keep logical Run occurrence identity/display format and sequence allocation open; this correction is only for the physical repository address boundary.
nonRequirements: No production implementation is required in revise-explore.
No Windows whole-manager Full Test is required at this boundary.
No symlink/junction/reparse-point hardening is added by this finding.
No Result admission, Policy, scheduler, database/WAL, or multi-Agent recovery work is required.

limitations: This is Review Explore only; it is neither Verification PASS nor Owner authority.

The detached reviewer host is Linux; the Windows reserved-name finding is grounded in Win32 naming rules plus independent lexical-gate reproduction, not a Windows filesystem write test.

Symlink/junction/reparse-point containment remains outside this finding, consistent with the revised Explore limitation.
